- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–10 days.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 2–5% to align with mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.10) and price is trending upward, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slightly (1–2%) to reflect sentiment lag.  
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the following 3–5 days; apply a 2–4% downward correction to avoid overreaction.  
- Model underestimates long-term mean reversion (especially after 15–20 days); add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast from day 15 onward if sentiment is weak or neutral.
